data_points.claim: Backpropagation computes the gradient of the cost with respect to every weight — the relative size of each nudge — not a verbal explanation of the mistake.
One training example produces a list of desired weight changes; SGD averages those across a mini-batch because full-batch gradients are too slow.
On a computational graph, each gate multiplies its local gradient by the upstream gradient — the chain rule is just walking the graph backward.
The size of ∂C/∂a is proportional to how far the output is from the label, so a big miss produces a bigger first nudge.

common_questions: Is a neural network just memorizing the training set?
What is a loss function actually measuring?
Does backpropagation tell the network *why* it was wrong?
What is a weight, in one sentence?

misconceptions.myth: The network understands the mistake the way a student does.
misconceptions.reality: It only receives a number (loss) and a direction for each knob (the gradient).
Learning means changing weights so future guesses are less wrong.
misconceptions.source: CS231n / Nielsen Neural Networks and Deep Learning

audience_insights.knowledge_level: Curious general audience; may have heard 'AI' and 'training' but not forward pass vs backprop.
pain_points: First explainers jump to calculus before the loop is visible.
Brain metaphors hide the actual algorithm.

expert_voices.name: Grant Sanderson
expert_voices.position: Learning is finding weights that minimize a cost; backprop is the algorithm that computes that gradient.

expert_voices.name: Andrej Karpathy
expert_voices.position: You want to see the loss go down as the only honest proof the network is learning.

angles_discovered.name: Guess, number, nudge
angles_discovered.hook: It does not memorize. It guesses, then turns the miss into a number.
angles_discovered.why_now: Saturated brain metaphors leave a 60s gap for the actual training loop.

angles_discovered.name: Loss is a compass, not a scolding
angles_discovered.hook: The network never hears 'wrong.' It only gets a number with a direction.
angles_discovered.why_now: Forum threads still ask if the model 'knows why' it failed.

angles_discovered.name: The chain rule as a walk backward
angles_discovered.hook: Error does not jump to the first layer. It walks back, gate by gate.
angles_discovered.why_now: CS231n already teaches this; motion is what the notes cannot do.

visual_references.what_works: One consistent diagram that changes state instead of cutting to new metaphors.

research_summary: The best explainers already exist as long math lessons. The gap is a 60-second teacher-explainer that refuses the brain metaphor and shows one loop: guess, score the miss as a number, walk the error backward, nudge the weights.
